pageTitle: Using Multi-Region Access Points with supported API operations
whatThePageStates: The page is mostly a how-to walkthrough for Amazon S3 Multi-Region Access Points (MRAPs), built from tabbed AWS CLI / SDK for Java / SDK for JavaScript / SDK for Python code examples for seven tasks (view routing configuration, update the underlying bucket policy, update a route configuration, PutObject, GetObject, ListObjectsV2, presigned URLs, Requester Pays). Inside that walkthrough there are three genuine enumerated coverage statements. First, under 'Multi-Region Access Point compatibility with S3 operations', a bullet list of 21 S3 data plane API operations that 'can accept Multi-Region Access Point ARNs', followed by a Note that copy operations are supported only with a MRAP as the destination. Second, in the same section, a bullet list of 9 S3 control plane operations you can use 'to create and manage your Multi-Region Access Points'. Third, under 'Update a Multi-Region Access Point route configuration', a bullet list of the five AWS Regions that MRAP route commands can be run against. The page states no negatives beyond the copy-operation qualifier and the SigV4A global-STS-endpoint warning; SDK compatibility itself is explicitly delegated to an off-page link (the AWS SDKs Reference), so this page makes no SDK or language coverage claim of its own.

features.featureName: Multi-Region Access Point compatibility with S3 operations (data plane operations that accept Multi-Region Access Point ARNs)
features.statuses: 21 Yes, 0 No, 0 Partial in the list itself; 21+0+0=21. Every bullet is an unqualified 'can accept Multi-Region Access Point ARNs' Yes: AbortMultipartUpload, CompleteMultipartUpload, CreateMultipartUpload, DeleteObject, DeleteObjectTagging, GetObject, GetObjectAcl, GetObjectLegalHold, GetObjectRetention, GetObjectTagging, HeadObject, ListMultipartUploads, ListObjectsV2, ListParts, PutObject, PutObjectAcl, PutObjectLegalHold, PutObjectRetention, PutObjectTagging, RestoreObject, UploadPart. No operation is listed as unsupported: every other S3 API operation is merely absent, which is not a coverage claim. One tri-state edge sits OUTSIDE the list: the Note after it says MRAPs support copy operations 'only as a destination when using the Multi-Region Access Point ARN' — a Partial for CopyObject/UploadPartCopy, which appear in no bullet. A parser that reads bullets gets 21; a parser that also credits the prose Partial could argue 22 with 1 Partial. The bullet count is 21.
features.scope: None per operation. A page-level qualifier applies to the whole list: these are data plane requests, for which 'Regions don't need to be specified'. There is no per-Region, per-plan or per-storage-class split for any individual operation.
features.reasoning: The enumerated axis is the AWS API operation name, and the unit of claim is 'this operation accepts a Multi-Region Access Point ARN'. apiOperation is a catalogue axis because the values are S3's own published API surface, not a universe that exists independently of S3. Data plane and control plane are kept as separate features because the two lists assert different things: the data plane list says an existing S3 object operation will accept a MRAP ARN in place of a bucket name, while the control plane list is the MRAP management API itself. Merging them into one count of 30 would blur two different claims.

features.featureName: Amazon S3 control plane operations to create and manage Multi-Region Access Points
features.statuses: 9 Yes, 0 No, 0 Partial; 9+0+0=9. CreateMultiRegionAccessPoint, DescribeMultiRegionAccessPointOperation, GetMultiRegionAccessPoint, GetMultiRegionAccessPointPolicy, GetMultiRegionAccessPointPolicyStatus, GetMultiRegionAccessPointRoutes, ListMultiRegionAccessPoints, PutMultiRegionAccessPointPolicy, SubmitMultiRegionAccessPointRoutes. Every bullet is an unqualified Yes. Note that DeleteMultiRegionAccessPoint and DeleteMultiRegionAccessPointPolicy are absent from the list — absence, not an explicit No, so this page makes no claim about them.
features.scope: Region endpoint, stated in prose rather than per row. All control plane requests to create or maintain a MRAP must be routed to US West (Oregon); the failover control plane (the two route operations) must be routed to one of five supported Regions. The prose also notes which operations are synchronous versus asynchronous, and that DescribeMultiRegionAccessPointOperation is always synchronous — a behaviour split, not a support split.
features.reasoning: Same axis and axisKind as the data plane feature: S3's own published API operation names. The unit of claim here is 'this operation is part of the Multi-Region Access Point management API', which is a different assertion from 'this operation accepts a MRAP ARN', so it is counted as its own feature.

features.featureName: Regions that Multi-Region Access Point route commands can be run against (failover control plane)
features.statuses: 5 Yes, 0 No, 0 Partial; 5+0+0=5. The sentence is explicit — 'Multi-Region Access Point route commands can be run against the following five Regions' — followed by bullets ap-southeast-2, ap-northeast-1, us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1. All other AWS Regions are simply not listed; the page states no exclusion for them and points elsewhere (MultiRegionAccessPointRestrictions) for MRAP supported Regions, so this is a Yes-only list and not a full supported/unsupported Region matrix.
features.scope: Applies only to the route (failover) control plane operations GetMultiRegionAccessPointRoutes and SubmitMultiRegionAccessPointRoutes. It is NOT the Region list for MRAPs generally, NOT the list of Regions whose buckets can back a MRAP, and NOT the general control plane endpoint — the page says that separately, and it is US West (Oregon) alone.
features.reasoning: The axis is the AWS Region, which exists independently of S3, so it is external. The unit of claim is 'a MRAP route command can be issued against this Region', a narrow endpoint-availability claim. Five values are named and the page itself says 'five', so the count is self-confirming.

shouldNotExtract: The 10-bullet 'Topics' navigation list at the top is a table of contents, not coverage. The tabbed example headers — 'AWS CLI', 'SDK for Java', 'SDK for JavaScript', 'SDK for Python' — are example flavours, not a programmingLanguage or SDK support matrix: they are unevenly present (four tabs for routing/PutObject/GetObject/ListObjectsV2, three for presigned URLs, two for Requester Pays, one JSON tab for the bucket policy), and the page explicitly delegates real SDK compatibility to an external link. Region strings inside code samples (ca-central-1, us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-2, US_EAST_1) are placeholder example values, not supported-Region claims. IAM action strings inside the example bucket policy JSON (s3:GetObject, s3:PutObject, s3:DeleteObject, s3:ListBucket) are policy content, not an operation-support list, and neither are the prose permission requirements (s3:ListAllMyBuckets, s3:PutObject, s3:GetObject, s3:ListBucket) in the Notes. The TrafficDialPercentage 100/0 active-passive explanation is configuration semantics, not coverage. The Notes about console synchrony, presigned URL expiry and the SigV4A/global-STS-endpoint error are caveats, not enumerable values. The trailing 'See also — Skills for AI coding assistants' Agent Toolkit boilerplate is site-wide footer text and carries no coverage at all.
coverageDimensions: REGION: the page gives exactly one enumerated Region figure — the five Regions for MRAP route commands (ap-southeast-2, ap-northeast-1, us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1) — plus one prose single-Region endpoint statement, that all MRAP create/maintain control plane requests go to US West (Oregon). It gives NO list of Regions where MRAPs are available, NO list of Regions whose buckets can back a MRAP, and no per-Region status for any API operation; for that it points off-page to MultiRegionAccessPointRestrictions. SERVICE: nothing. The page is entirely about one service, Amazon S3, and the only cross-service section ('compatibility with AWS services and AWS SDKs') enumerates nothing — it is two sentences that hand the reader an external link. Any per-service count taken from this page is fabricated. RESOURCE TYPE: nothing enumerated. The resources named in prose (buckets, objects, Multi-Region Access Points) are the subject matter, not an enumerated supported-resource-type list, and there is no resource type matrix of any kind.
trap: The single most likely misparse is treating the two operation bullet lists as one list and reporting 30 operations for a single feature, or conversely reporting only the first 21 and dropping the control plane list because it sits under the same H2 heading with no heading of its own. Runners-up: (1) harvesting the four tabbed code-example headers (AWS CLI, SDK for Java, SDK for JavaScript, SDK for Python) as a programmingLanguage or SDK coverage axis, which would invent an SDK support matrix this page deliberately does not publish, and would produce an inconsistent count because the tab set differs per section; (2) sweeping every Region-looking string on the page and reporting 6+ supported Regions, because ca-central-1 appears only as a placeholder in Java and JavaScript route-update samples — the real answer is the 5 bulleted Regions; (3) reading the Note 'supports copy operations ... only as a destination' as an unqualified Yes for CopyObject and adding it to the data plane list, when it is a Partial stated in prose and CopyObject has no bullet; (4) mining the example bucket policy JSON and the permission Notes for s3:* action names and mixing them into the API operation count; (5) treating the 10-bullet Topics table of contents as an enumerated feature list.
